items.text: Application allowlisting blocks an unapproved executable before it starts.
items.explanation: The control stops unauthorized software execution before the event occurs.

items.text: A monitoring rule alerts on an unexpected privileged sign-in.
items.explanation: The alert identifies activity that has occurred or is occurring.

items.text: A system restores a protected known-good configuration after an unauthorized change.
items.explanation: The restoration repairs the affected state after the change.

items.text: A sign states that access is monitored and unauthorized entry may be prosecuted.
items.explanation: The warning is intended to discourage an attempted violation.

items.text: Verify a user with a registered passkey before sign-in.
items.explanation: The passkey is used to verify the identity claiming the account.

items.text: Permit the Finance Approver role to release payments up to its assigned limit.
items.explanation: The role and limit determine what an authenticated user is permitted to do.

items.text: Record which administrator changed a firewall rule and when the change occurred.
items.explanation: The audit record creates a history of accountable actions.

items.text: Validate a user certificate from a smart card during login.
items.explanation: Certificate validation contributes to verifying the user identity.

items.text: Block a Sales role from opening employee medical-benefit records.
items.explanation: The access decision restricts what the authenticated role may read.

items.text: Write timestamped records of privileged API changes to the audit system.
items.explanation: The records support accountability and later review of privileged actions.

items.text: Assess the security and operational impact of the proposed rule change.
items.explanation: Impact analysis identifies affected services, risks, dependencies, and rollback needs before authorization.

items.text: Obtain authorization from the designated change approver.
items.explanation: The assessed change must be authorized before the approved work proceeds.

items.text: Test the approved rule change in the designated nonproduction environment.
items.explanation: Testing checks the intended behavior before the production system is changed.

items.text: Implement the approved and tested rule change in production.
items.explanation: Production implementation follows approval and testing.

items.text: Validate the result and update the change and configuration records.
items.explanation: Post-change validation confirms the outcome and records the resulting production state.

items.text: One external source tries the same password once against many employee accounts.
items.explanation: Password spraying spreads a small number of password guesses across many accounts to avoid per-account lockouts.

items.text: A host sends frequent DNS queries containing long, high-entropy subdomain labels.
items.explanation: Encoded or high-entropy labels can carry command-and-control or exfiltration data through DNS.

items.text: A payroll sign-in link uses a domain that differs from the company domain by one character.
items.explanation: Typosquatting uses lookalike or misspelled domains to deceive users.

items.text: A memory image shows a privileged process that normal operating-system tools do not display.
items.explanation: Rootkits can conceal processes, drivers, files, or other artifacts from normal system tools.

items.text: An API verifies sign-in but does not verify that the user may access the requested customer record.
items.explanation: The missing per-object authorization check is an application-logic weakness.

items.text: A cloud storage bucket containing internal reports is configured for public read access.
items.explanation: The unsafe access setting exposes data because of configuration rather than application logic.

items.text: A trusted vendor build pipeline is compromised and distributes a modified signed update to customers.
items.explanation: The weakness enters through a trusted supplier development and distribution process.

items.text: A web application concatenates untrusted input directly into a database query.
items.explanation: Unsafe query construction is an application weakness that can enable injection.

items.text: A newly deployed appliance still uses the vendor default administrator password.
items.explanation: Leaving a default credential in place is an insecure configuration state.

items.text: A dependency package is pulled automatically after the package publisher account is compromised.
items.explanation: A compromised upstream package source introduces risk through the software supply chain.

items.text: Register or prepare the lookalike sign-in site.
items.explanation: The deceptive destination must exist before victims can be sent to it.

items.text: Send the user a message containing the deceptive sign-in link.
items.explanation: The lure directs the user to the attacker-controlled site.

items.text: Capture the credentials the user submits to the lookalike page.
items.explanation: The attacker obtains the password only after the victim enters it.

items.text: Submit the stolen credentials to the legitimate service.
items.explanation: The captured credentials are then used against the real authentication service.

items.text: Establish an authenticated session to the victim account.
items.explanation: Account access follows successful use of the stolen credentials.

items.text: The customer must manage the guest operating system, host firewall, and installed agents.
items.explanation: IaaS leaves guest operating systems and deployed software under customer control.

items.text: Developers deploy application code while the provider manages the operating system and application runtime.
items.explanation: PaaS provides the managed platform while customers deploy and secure their application code and data.

items.text: Users consume a finished business application through a browser without managing its platform.
items.explanation: SaaS delivers the completed application as the provider-managed service.

items.text: A short event-driven function runs on demand without the customer maintaining servers.
items.explanation: Serverless execution abstracts server operation while the customer supplies the function code and configuration.

items.text: An encrypted payroll file stored on an endpoint SSD.
items.explanation: The file is stored on persistent media and is therefore at rest.

items.text: An API request protected by TLS while crossing the Internet.
items.explanation: The request is moving between systems over a network.

items.text: A customer record decrypted in application memory while a calculation is performed.
items.explanation: The record is actively being processed in memory.

items.text: An encrypted database backup stored on offline media.
items.explanation: The backup is stored rather than being transmitted or processed.

items.text: Replication traffic protected by IPsec between two sites.
items.explanation: The replication data is moving through a protected network tunnel.

items.text: Decrypted transaction values loaded into memory for an analytics job.
items.explanation: The values are actively processed by the analytics workload.

items.text: Declare the primary site unavailable and activate the recovery plan.
items.explanation: The recovery process begins after the incident meets the criteria for declaring the primary site unavailable.

items.text: Activate the required compute, network, and access services at the warm site.
items.explanation: The alternate environment must be ready before application data and services are restored.

items.text: Restore or synchronize the approved recovery data to the alternate environment.
items.explanation: The applications need the required recovery data before functional validation.

items.text: Validate the critical application and security controls at the warm site.
items.explanation: Testing verifies that the recovered service and protections operate correctly before users are redirected.

items.text: Redirect user and application traffic to the validated warm-site service.
items.explanation: Traffic moves only after the alternate service has been validated.

items.text: A process tree shows a document reader spawning a script interpreter on one laptop.
items.explanation: Endpoint detection and response tools collect process and host activity from endpoints.

items.text: A network alert identifies an exploit signature in traffic crossing a monitored segment.
items.explanation: IDS and IPS technologies inspect network traffic for suspicious or known attack patterns.

items.text: An alert combines identity, endpoint, and firewall events into one correlated incident.
items.explanation: A SIEM aggregates and correlates events from multiple security sources.

items.text: An outbound upload is blocked because the file contains regulated identifiers.
items.explanation: DLP identifies sensitive information and can enforce rules that restrict its movement.

items.text: Send a signed identity assertion from an identity provider to a service provider for browser SSO.
items.explanation: SAML is designed to exchange authentication and attribute assertions between identity and service providers.

items.text: Let a user authorize an application to access a limited API scope without giving the application the user password.
items.explanation: OAuth supports delegated authorization through scoped access tokens.

items.text: Query a centralized directory for user and group attributes.
items.explanation: LDAP is commonly used to access and manage directory information.

items.text: Require an authenticator designed to resist credential replay through a fake sign-in site.
items.explanation: Phishing-resistant authenticators bind authentication to the legitimate verifier or origin.

items.text: A credentialed scanner discovers that a server is missing a security update.
items.explanation: The scan identifies a potential vulnerability.

items.text: Threat intelligence shows active exploitation of a public-facing vulnerability on a critical system.
items.explanation: Exploit activity, exposure, and asset importance influence treatment priority.

items.text: Administrators deploy the vendor security update to the affected servers.
items.explanation: Applying the update changes the vulnerable state and is a remediation action.

items.text: The team rescans the servers after deployment to confirm the finding is gone.
items.explanation: The rescan checks whether remediation successfully removed the vulnerability.

items.text: A penetration tester discovers an authorization flaw that the automated scanner missed.
items.explanation: The manual test identifies an additional weakness.

items.text: The team raises a finding because the affected asset processes regulated customer data.
items.explanation: Asset sensitivity changes the relative urgency of treatment.

items.text: A firewall rule blocks the exposed vulnerable service until the permanent fix is ready.
items.explanation: The compensating change reduces exposure and is a remediation or mitigation action.

items.text: Testing confirms that the temporary block prevents access from untrusted networks.
items.explanation: The test verifies that the applied control has the intended effect.

items.text: Successful sign-in with the username, MFA result, source address, and timestamp.
items.explanation: Authentication systems directly record identity and sign-in events.

items.text: A DNS query from an internal host to a newly observed external domain.
items.explanation: DNS and network monitoring provide evidence about host communications.

items.text: A document reader spawns a script interpreter with a suspicious command line.
items.explanation: Endpoint telemetry records process creation and command-line activity.

items.text: An administrator changes a cloud storage bucket policy to allow public access.
items.explanation: Cloud control-plane audit logs record administrative resource changes.

items.text: Repeated failed sign-ins for one account from several source addresses.
items.explanation: The identity system is the direct source for authentication outcomes.

items.text: A proxy records a large HTTPS upload to an unsanctioned file-sharing domain.
items.explanation: Web proxy data records destination, user or device context, and transfer details.

items.text: An endpoint sensor quarantines a file and records its hash and parent process.
items.explanation: Endpoint security telemetry records file and process activity on the host.

items.text: A cloud administrator grants a new privileged role to a service identity.
items.explanation: The cloud audit trail records identity and policy changes made through the control plane.

items.text: Preparation
items.explanation: Preparation establishes the people, tools, communications, and procedures needed before an incident.

items.text: Detection and analysis
items.explanation: Detection and analysis determine whether an event is an incident and establish scope and impact.

items.text: Containment
items.explanation: Containment limits additional damage and spread before the threat is removed.

items.text: Eradication
items.explanation: Eradication removes malicious code, persistence, and exploited weaknesses after containment.

items.text: Recovery
items.explanation: Recovery restores and validates normal operations after the threat has been removed.

items.text: Lessons learned and improvement
items.explanation: Post-incident review identifies improvements to controls, procedures, and training.

items.text: Submit the privileged-access request with the maintenance purpose and time window.
items.explanation: The workflow begins with a documented business need and requested duration.

items.text: Obtain approval from the designated privileged-access owner.
items.explanation: Authorization is required before elevated rights are granted.

items.text: Have PAM grant the approved administrator role for the limited window.
items.explanation: PAM activates only the privilege authorized for the approved period.

items.text: Perform the maintenance while the privileged session is logged or recorded.
items.explanation: The approved access is used with accountability during the maintenance activity.

items.text: Automatically remove the elevated role when the approved window expires.
items.explanation: Automatic removal prevents the temporary privilege from becoming standing access.

items.text: States management direction that sensitive company data must be protected.
items.explanation: A policy establishes high-level management intent and expectations.

items.text: Requires approved encryption algorithms and minimum key sizes for protected data.
items.explanation: A standard defines specific mandatory requirements used to implement policy.

items.text: Lists the steps the service desk follows to create and verify a new employee account.
items.explanation: A procedure provides repeatable step-by-step instructions for performing an activity.

items.text: Recommends safer practices employees should consider when using networks while traveling.
items.explanation: A guideline provides recommended practices and allows situational judgment.

items.text: Discontinue an optional Internet-facing service that creates more risk than business value.
items.explanation: Ending the activity removes the source of that risk.

items.text: Purchase cyber insurance to cover part of the financial impact of a qualifying incident.
items.explanation: Insurance transfers a defined portion of financial impact to the insurer under the policy terms.

items.text: Require phishing-resistant authentication for administrators to reduce account-compromise likelihood.
items.explanation: The control reduces the likelihood or impact of the identified threat.

items.text: Document and approve a low residual risk that falls within the established tolerance.
items.explanation: The organization knowingly retains the remaining risk after review.

items.text: Remove an unnecessary data-collection feature so the organization no longer stores that sensitive field.
items.explanation: Removing the activity eliminates the associated storage and exposure risk.

items.text: Use a contract that assigns specified financial responsibility to a service provider for defined failures.
items.explanation: The contract shifts specified consequences to another party, although the organization still retains some risk.

items.text: Segment and closely monitor a legacy system while its replacement is being completed.
items.explanation: The temporary controls reduce exposure without eliminating the underlying system risk.

items.text: A risk owner formally accepts a small remaining exposure until the planned replacement date.
items.explanation: The owner acknowledges and retains the residual risk for the approved period.

items.text: Define the security, privacy, resilience, and data-handling requirements for the service.
items.explanation: Requirements must be known before the organization can evaluate candidate providers.

items.text: Assess the provider and important subcontractors against the defined requirements.
items.explanation: Due diligence evaluates whether the provider can meet the required controls and obligations.

items.text: Execute the agreement with required security clauses, service targets, notification terms, and assurance rights.
items.explanation: Contractual obligations should be established before access and regulated processing begin.

items.text: Provision only the approved access and data flows needed for the contracted service.
items.explanation: Onboarding implements the least-privilege connection after the relationship is approved and contracted.

items.text: Monitor performance, control evidence, incidents, material changes, and supplier risk during the relationship.
items.explanation: Ongoing monitoring addresses changes that occur after the initial assessment.

items.text: Revoke access and complete required data return, retention, or verified destruction when the relationship ends.
items.explanation: Termination activities remove access and resolve data obligations at the end of the lifecycle.
